headline: Ahead of Special Town Meeting, Southborough boards finalized competing recommendations on trail funding, golf course irrigation, water extensions, and two-family zoning.
synopsis: In October 2026, Southborough town boards focused heavily on final preparations and recommendations for the October 17 Special Town Meeting. The Advisory Committee and Community Preservation Committee diverged on major funding requests, with the Advisory Committee recommending against additional CPA money for the Peninsula Trail bridge and golf course irrigation due to high costs. Meanwhile, the Advisory Committee unanimously endorsed spending $240,000 from water reserves to connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill to municipal water. Zoning for two-family dwellings also generated debate, securing unanimous support from the Zoning Board of Appeals but an unfavorable recommendation from the Advisory Committee. In other municipal business, the Select Board reviewed an initial assessment of the town's governance structure, and departments began advancing their FY28 budget requests.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail Footbridge Funding
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send a $217,318 CPA funding request to Special Town Meeting, despite unanimous opposition from the Advisory Committee over project costs.
top_items.body: Article 4 requests $217,318 in new Community Preservation Act funds to supplement $211,000 previously approved for a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian bridge along Route 30, bringing the total project cost to $428,550. The Advisory Committee opposed the appropriation due to the estimated cost of roughly $5,000 per linear foot. After evaluating potential floor amendments to scale back the request, both the Community Preservation Committee and the Trails Committee decided to advance the article as printed.

top_items.title: Golf Course Irrigation System Financing
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee recommended against using Community Preservation Act funds for a $1 million golf course irrigation project, while the Golf Committee resolved to present the request intact.
top_items.body: The Southborough Golf Club project requires roughly $1.08 million, combining previously approved CPA funds, $100,000 from the golf revolving fund, and $433,546 in additional CPA money. The Advisory Committee opposed shifting capital expenses onto CPA funds, stating that the municipal course was intended to be self-sustaining. The Golf Committee voted to spend up to $500 on informational flyers and agreed by consensus to present the article as written without seeking floor amendments.

top_items.title: Water Line Connections Near Parkerville Landfill
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Town Meeting approve $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill to town water.
top_items.body: Article 7 addresses contamination testing near the town landfill by extending the municipal water main to two affected properties. The Advisory Committee confirmed that the town will fund both the street main extension and the private service lines into the houses using water enterprise retained earnings.

top_items.title: Two-Family Housing Zoning Proposal
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support a two-family dwelling zoning amendment as written, while the Advisory Committee issued an unfavorable recommendation.
top_items.body: The proposed zoning change would amend bylaws governing two-family dwellings. The Zoning Board of Appeals opted against last-minute revisions and voted to move forward with the draft warrant language. The Advisory Committee voted against recommending the measure, raising concerns over lot sizes in Residential B zones, property flipping following the removal of a two-year ownership requirement, and reliance on percolation tests for septic capacity.

top_items.title: Stormwater Enterprise Fund Authorization
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee clarified that Warrant Article 5 establishes an accounting mechanism for stormwater management but does not implement any user fees.
top_items.body: Article 5 seeks to create a dedicated stormwater enterprise fund under state statute. The Advisory Committee emphasized in its warrant report that creating the fund structure will not impose fees on residents without future Town Meeting approval, but could eventually allow the town to distribute stormwater costs based on impervious surface areas across all parcels, including tax-exempt properties.

top_items.title: Municipal Governance Structure Review
top_items.why: Consultant Bill Keegan presented an initial assessment to the Select Board examining Southborough's governance model, committee oversight, and town manager authority.
top_items.body: The presentation launched an administrative study comparing Southborough's municipal operations and committee structures against peer Massachusetts communities. The review is evaluating administrative roles, statutory authority, and potential structural adjustments to town government.
